newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia drought a concern for GDP - Fahey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia drought a concern for GDP - Fahey.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Monday the drought affecting most of Australia was a concern for the government's economic growth forecasts.
But that the government was still on track for a budget surplus as forecast in its budget for the 1997/98 year.

"It's a concern," Fahey told reporters, when asked about the possible effects of the drought on the government's forecast for gross domestic product (GDP) to rise 3.75 percent through the year to June 30, 1998.

The government has forecast a headline budget surplus of A$6.42 billion for 1997/98, but an underlying deficit of A$3.85 billion. For 1998/99, the government has forecast a underlying surplus of A$1.6 billion and a headline suprlus of A$6.78 billion.
The 1996/97 year ended in an underlying budget deficit of A$4.93 billion, much better than forecasts for an underlying A$6.86 billion shortfall.

Fahey said provisional data for the just ended 1996/97 year indicated "very clearly that we are well and truly on target for a surplus of A$1.6 billion as forecast in this year's budget -- a surplus in next year's budget."
"The treasurer said a week ago comprehensively there is some concern about a return to drought and what impact that will have on the budget and on Australia's capacity to export," he said.
"It's a concern and it's something the government is keeping a close eye on," Fahey said.
